security_review.reason: This slice's entire purpose is correcting the serialization guarantee of a privilege-boundary bootstrap for two cluster-global, BYPASSRLS-capable roles, and its design deliberately runs in a DEGRADED, unserialized mode on the confirmed-real production host (DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL never grants superuser). Security round must specifically verify: (1) the exception handler catches ONLY insufficient_privilege (SQLSTATE 42501) around the LOCK TABLE statement -- any broader WHEN clause (e.g. WHEN OTHERS) would silently swallow unrelated failures and must be rejected; (2) the RAISE WARNING text is unconditionally emitted on that specific failure and is not itself gated behind some condition that could suppress it; (3) SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE is the mode actually used, not a stronger mode that would newly block ordinary GRANT/REVOKE cluster-wide, nor a weaker mode that would not self-conflict; (4) chat-definer.sql's removed comment block is exactly the pg_advisory_xact_lock rationale (including the now-disproven SERIALIZABLE claim) and no adjacent, still-valid comment (attribute-drift rationale, re-pointing guard rationale) was accidentally removed alongside it; (5) neither file's attributes, fail-closed checks, or (chat_definer) re-pointing guard changed; (6) the new migrate.test.ts concurrency cases genuinely exercise cross-database concurrency (two distinct database connections, Promise.all, not sequential awaits) and would fail if the LOCK TABLE statement were removed -- ask the implementer to demonstrate this via the one-time mutation-test check named in slice doc S7.4; (7) the new degraded-privilege test case actually connects as a non-superuser role shaped like DigitalOcean's documented doadmin attributes, not merely asserts the warning text without exercising the real permission boundary.

_note: Authored 2026-08-05 in an authoring-only session (no register, no worktree, no implementation), then revised the same day after owner review resolved the production-privilege question. Two rounds of live experimentation informed this contract. Round 1 (mechanism selection, slice doc S5): two of the three candidates named in the already-merged deferral (docs/autopilot-chat-definer-role-provisioning.md SS10 item 8) were tested against this session's local Postgres 16 cluster and found NOT to work as documented -- SERIALIZABLE isolation does not detect the cross-database conflict, and a row-level FOR UPDATE lock on a shared catalog row does not block cross-database despite the catalog's storage being physically shared. The chosen mechanism (relation-level LOCK TABLE) was cross-checked for three separate properties: that it blocks cross-database (it does), that it does not block ordinary GRANT/REVOKE elsewhere (it does not), and what privilege it requires (confirmed superuser-only via three separate negative tests). Round 2 (production-privilege resolution, slice doc S5.4.1/S5.4.2), triggered by owner feedback confirming DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL never grants superuser: built a scratch role mirroring doadmin's own documented attribute set (fetched from DigitalOcean's own docs, not assumed) and ran the full bootstrap sequence under it end to end, which both confirmed the fail-open design works as intended AND surfaced a second, previously-unconsidered finding -- PostgreSQL 16 auto-grants a CREATEROLE-holding creator membership in any role it creates, a side effect invisible in every environment this repo runs today because the real credential there is a true superuser. All scratch roles, tables, and databases created during both rounds of experimentation were dropped before this manifest was authored.
